title: Jacob, Rachel, Leah and Joseph
bigQuestion: What does the Torah say happened to Jacob's family, and how did the twelve tribes get their names?

story.title: A Ladder to the Sky
story.kicker: A young man sleeps on a stone and dreams of a ladder that goes all the way up.
paragraphs: It is night. A young man named Jacob is far from home. He is alone. He has no bed. The Torah says he puts a stone under his head. He lies down on the ground. He falls asleep.
Jacob dreams. In the dream, there is a ladder. Its bottom is on the earth. Its top reaches the sky. Angels are going up the ladder. Angels are coming down. Up and down, up and down.
In the dream, the story says, God speaks to Jacob. "I am with you. I will keep you safe. I will bring you back to this land." It is the same promise God made to Abraham.
Jacob wakes up. He is amazed. "God was here," he says, "and I did not know it!" He sets up the stone. He names the place Beth-el. That means "house of God."
story.think: Jacob was alone and far from home. How do you think the dream made him feel?

lessons.title: Jacob and Esau
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Isaac and Rebekah had twin sons, Jacob and Esau, who did not get along.
reading: Isaac and Rebekah had *twins*. Twins are two babies born together. The first was Esau. He was red and hairy. The second was Jacob. He was holding Esau's heel.
The boys grew up very different. Esau liked to hunt outside. Jacob liked to stay near the tents. The Torah says the brothers had a big fight over a blessing.
Esau was angry. Jacob had to leave home. He went far away to his uncle Laban. He did not see his brother for a long, long time.

words.d: two babies born together from the same mother; Jacob and Esau were twins
Jacob's twin brother; the Torah says he was born first

look.title: Two Very Different Brothers
look.text: Picture two boys who are twins. One has red hair all over his arms. He carries a bow and runs to the fields. The other stays by the tents and cooks a pot of red stew. They are brothers, but they are not the same.
look.prompt: The Torah says the twins were very different. What is one way you are different from someone in your family?

check.q: Who were Jacob and Esau's parents?
check.why: Genesis 25 says Isaac and Rebekah had twin sons, Esau and Jacob.

check.q: Which twin was born first?
check.why: Esau was born first. Jacob came second, holding Esau's heel.

check.q: Why did Jacob leave home?
choices: He wanted to see the sea
His brother was angry with him
check.why: After the fight over the blessing, Esau was angry, so Jacob went to his uncle Laban.

lessons.title: The Ladder Dream
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob dreamed of a ladder to the sky with angels going up and down.
reading: On his trip, Jacob slept outside. He used a stone for a pillow. The Torah says he had a dream. He saw a *ladder*. It went from the ground to the sky.
Angels went up the ladder. Angels came down. In the dream, God made Jacob a promise. "I am with you. I will bring you back home."
Jacob woke up. He named the place Beth-el. Beth-el means "house of God." Jewish tradition says the dream showed Jacob he was not alone.

words.d: a tall set of steps you climb; Jacob dreamed of one that reached the sky
the name Jacob gave the place where he dreamed; it means "house of God"

look.title: A Ladder Set Up on the Earth
look.text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
look.prompt: "Ascending" means going up. "Descending" means going down. Show with your hand what the angels were doing.

check.q: What did Jacob see in his dream?
check.why: Genesis 28 says Jacob dreamed of a ladder from the earth to the sky. The boat and rainbow are in Noah's story.

check.q: What did Jacob use for a pillow?
check.why: The Torah says Jacob put a stone under his head and went to sleep.

check.q: What does Beth-el mean?
check.why: Beth-el means "house of God." Jacob named the place after his dream. "He laughs" is Isaac's name.

lessons.title: Rachel and Leah
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob worked many years for Laban and married both Leah and Rachel.
reading: Jacob came to his uncle Laban. Laban had two daughters. Leah was the older one. *Rachel* was the younger one. Jacob met Rachel at a well. He loved her.
Jacob said, "I will work for you seven years. Then let me marry Rachel." Laban said yes. But at the wedding, Laban gave him *Leah* instead. Jacob was tricked!
Jacob worked seven more years. Then he married Rachel too. In those days, a man could have more than one wife. Both Leah and Rachel are called mothers of the family.

words.d: Laban's younger daughter; the Torah says Jacob loved her and met her at a well
Laban's older daughter; the Torah says Jacob married her first

look.title: Jacob Works for Laban
rows: Years Jacob worked before he married Leah
More years he worked for Rachel
look.unit: years, as the Torah tells it
look.prompt: The Torah says seven years felt like a few days to Jacob because he loved Rachel. What makes time feel fast for you?

check.q: Who was Laban?
check.why: Laban was Rebekah's brother, so he was Jacob's uncle. Esau was his twin.

check.q: How many years did Jacob first work to marry Rachel?
check.why: Genesis 29 says Jacob worked seven years, and then seven more.

check.q: Who did Laban give Jacob at the first wedding?
check.why: Laban gave him Leah, the older daughter. Jacob married Rachel later.

lessons.title: A New Name: Israel
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob wrestled all night with a stranger and got a new name, Israel.
reading: Many years went by. Jacob went home with his big family. He was afraid to see Esau. The night before, he was alone by a river.
The Torah says a stranger came. They *wrestled* all night. To wrestle is to grab and push and not let go. At dawn, the stranger said, "Let me go." Jacob said, "Not until you bless me."
The stranger gave Jacob a new name: *Israel*. The next day, Jacob met Esau. Esau ran to him. They hugged and cried. The brothers made peace.

words.d: to grab and push against someone and not let go
the new name the Torah says Jacob was given; his family became the people of Israel

look.title: Not Jacob, But Israel
look.text: The Torah says the stranger told Jacob: your name will not be Jacob anymore. It will be Israel. You have struggled with God and with people, and you have held on.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 32:29, retold from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Jacob got a new name after he held on all night. What is something hard you kept trying at?

check.q: What new name did Jacob get?
check.why: Genesis 32 says Jacob's new name was Israel. Esau is his brother and Isaac is his father.

check.q: What did Jacob do all night by the river?
check.why: The Torah says Jacob wrestled with a stranger until dawn.

check.q: What happened when Jacob met Esau again?
check.why: Genesis 33 says Esau ran to Jacob, hugged him, and they both cried.

lessons.title: Twelve Sons and Dinah
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob had twelve sons and a daughter, and the twelve tribes are named for his sons.
reading: Jacob had a very big family. The Torah says he had twelve sons. He also had a daughter. Her name was Dinah. Leah and Rachel were mothers of the family.
Some sons were Reuben, Judah, Levi and Joseph. Joseph was Rachel's son. Rachel's other son was Benjamin. He was the youngest of all.
Later, the family grew into a people. Jewish tradition says the people had twelve *tribes*. A tribe is a very big family group. The tribes were named for Jacob's sons.

words.d: a very big family group; the Torah names twelve tribes of Israel
Jacob and Leah's daughter, named in the Torah

look.title: Jacob's Children
look.cite: Genesis 29–30, 35:22–26 and 49:28, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: How many sons did Jacob have? How many tribes? What do you notice?

check.q: How many sons does the Torah say Jacob had?
check.why: Genesis says Jacob had twelve sons. The twelve tribes are named for them.

check.q: Who was Dinah?
check.why: Dinah was the daughter of Jacob and Leah. Rebekah was his mother.

check.q: What is a tribe?
check.why: A tribe is a very big family group. The people of Israel had twelve tribes.

lessons.title: The Coat and the Dreams
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Jacob gave Joseph a special coat, and Joseph's dreams made his brothers jealous.
reading: Jacob loved Joseph very much. The Torah says he gave Joseph a special *coat*. His brothers did not get one. They were *jealous*. To be jealous is to want what someone else has.
Joseph had dreams. In one, his brothers' bundles of wheat bowed to his bundle. In another, the sun, moon and stars bowed to him. Joseph told everyone. His brothers got even more angry.
One day the brothers were far away with the sheep. Jacob sent Joseph to check on them. The brothers saw him coming in his coat.

words.d: the special piece of clothing the Torah says Jacob gave Joseph
wanting what someone else has and feeling upset about it

look.title: Bundles That Bow
look.text: Picture a field at harvest. Wheat is tied in tall bundles. In Joseph's dream, his bundle stands up straight. All his brothers' bundles bend over and bow to it. Joseph tells his brothers the dream. They frown.
look.prompt: What do you think the brothers thought the dream meant? How would you feel if you were a brother?

check.q: What did Jacob give Joseph?
check.why: Genesis 37 says Jacob made Joseph a special coat, and his brothers were jealous.

check.q: What does jealous mean?
check.why: Jealous means wanting what someone else has. The brothers wanted Joseph's coat and their father's love.

check.q: In Joseph's dream, what bowed to his bundle of wheat?
check.why: In the dream, the brothers' bundles bowed to Joseph's bundle. The brothers did not like that.

lessons.title: Joseph in Egypt
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Joseph's brothers sold him, but in Egypt he became a great helper to the king.
reading: The brothers grabbed Joseph. They took his coat. They put him in a deep hole. Then they sold him to travelers going to *Egypt*. They told Jacob that Joseph was dead. Jacob cried and cried.
In Egypt, Joseph worked hard. But he was blamed for something he did not do. He was put in jail. In jail, he told people what their dreams meant.
The king of Egypt was called *Pharaoh*. Pharaoh had a strange dream. Joseph said it meant seven good years, then seven hungry years. Pharaoh made Joseph his top helper. Joseph saved up food.

words.d: a land by a big river where the Torah says Joseph was taken
the name for the king of Egypt

look.title: Pharaoh's Dream
rows: Good years with lots of food
look.prompt: Joseph told Pharaoh to save food in the good years. Why was that a smart plan?

check.q: What did the brothers do to Joseph?
choices: They sold him to travelers going to Egypt
check.why: Genesis 37 says the brothers sold Joseph to travelers who took him to Egypt.

check.q: Who is Pharaoh?
check.why: Pharaoh is the name for the king of Egypt. Joseph became his top helper.

check.q: What did Joseph say Pharaoh's dream meant?
choices: Seven good years, then seven hungry years
Pharaoh would get a new coat
check.why: Joseph said the dream meant seven years with lots of food and seven with little, so Egypt should save up.

lessons.title: Brothers Together Again
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Joseph forgave his brothers, and the whole family moved to Egypt.
reading: The hungry years came. Jacob's family had no food. The brothers went to Egypt to buy some. They stood in front of Joseph. They did not know him. He knew them.
Joseph tested them. Then he could not hold back. He cried. "I am Joseph!" he said. "Is my father still alive?" The brothers were scared. But Joseph said, "Do not be afraid."

Joseph *forgave* his brothers. To forgive is to stop being angry at someone. The whole family moved to Egypt. Jacob saw Joseph again. Jewish tradition says forgiving is one of the big lessons of this story.

words.d: to stop being angry at someone for what they did

look.title: You Meant It for Bad
look.text: The Torah says Joseph told his brothers: you planned something bad for me, but God turned it into something good, so that many people could be kept alive.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 50:20, retold from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Joseph chose to forgive. What is one kind thing you could say to someone who was mean to you?

check.q: Why did the brothers go to Egypt?
check.why: In the hungry years, the brothers went to Egypt to buy food.

check.q: What does forgive mean?
choices: To stop being angry at someone
To go on a long trip
check.why: To forgive is to stop being angry at someone. Joseph forgave his brothers.

check.q: Where did Jacob's whole family go at the end of the story?
check.why: Genesis 46 says Jacob and the whole family moved to Egypt to be near Joseph.

review.q: Who were the twins in this chapter?
review.why: Genesis 25 says Isaac and Rebekah had twins, Esau and Jacob.

review.q: What did Jacob see in his dream at Beth-el?
review.why: Genesis 28 says Jacob dreamed of a ladder to the sky with angels going up and down.

review.q: Which two sisters did Jacob marry?
review.why: Jacob married Leah first, then Rachel. They were Laban's daughters.
The Torah says the stranger gave Jacob the name Israel after they wrestled.

review.q: How did the twelve tribes get their names?
review.why: The twelve tribes of Israel are named for the sons of Jacob.

review.q: What did Joseph do when his brothers came to Egypt?
review.why: Genesis 45 says Joseph told them who he was, cried, and told them not to be afraid.
